scope: Proposition 4.4 (Cost of the shortened-beam construction) of the manuscript “Finite triangular approximation of radial sweeps” (preprints/Finite-triangular-approximation-of-radial-sweeps-September-27-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 100 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 6e7f63022190f390), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 12. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For a ∈ (0, 1/2), fix M = 25 in (4.5) and put C(a) = C1 + C2, with C1, C2 as in (4.3) and (4.10). For every ζ > 0, the tetrahedron K has a finite cylinder cover of normalized cost at most C(a)+ζ, consisting of cylinders with nondegenerate compact triangular perpendicular bases covering H− ∪ H+ and cylinders with horizontal axes and compact rectangular perpendicular bases covering G. Moreover, C(a) = 4 − √ 2 2 − 19 30 ! a2 + O(a3 ) (a ↓ 0). (4.11) In particular, sufficiently small a > 0 permits a finite cover whose actual total base area is strictly below Amin(K)/2.
